paper.title_en: Photon efficiency-coherence time product rule for NV-centre and trapped-ion quantum repeater chains
paper.abstract_en: The fidelity of a first-generation quantum repeater is controlled by a single hardware quantity, whose identification explains a striking equivalence between the two leading qubit platforms. By simulating nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre and trapped-ion ($^ {171}$Yb$^+$) repeater chains over an identical 200 km fibre channel-anchored to optical time-domain reflectometry field measurements of a deployed single-mode link and statistically extended to 66.08 dB total loss-we find that the two platforms deliver statistically indistinguishable raw fidelity at three segments (NV: $F_{\mathrm{tel}} = 0.605$; trapped ion: $F_{\mathrm{tel}} = 0.589$), despite five-fold opposite photon-efficiency and coherence-time specifications. A two-dimensional sensitivity analysis reveals why: at fixed channel loss, repeater fidelity is controlled by the product $\eta_{\mathrm{photon}}\!\cdot\!T_2$ of photon efficiency and coherence time, not by either quantity alone. Both platforms share $\eta_{\mathrm{photon}}\!\cdot\!T_2 = 0.20$ s and therefore perform identically; any two platforms on the same iso-product line will likewise coincide. This design rule yields a concrete hardware target: reaching the BB84 key-distribution threshold at three segments requires $\eta_{\mathrm{photon}}\!\cdot\!T_2 {\unicode{x2A7E}} 2.44$ s, a twelve-fold improvement, and at the throughput-optimal segment count gate and measurement errors cap fidelity near 0.806 regardless of memory quality. The comparison is built on the NetSquid discrete-event simulator with experimentally validated parameters, full three-basis state tomography, and density-matrix DEJMPS purification; the last reveals that realistic dephasing-biased chain states purify substantially better than the Werner-state recurrence predicts. Trapped ions purify more effectively (Bell fidelity 0.608 versus 0.509 after one round) owing to superior gate and readout fidelity, while NV centre generate entangled pairs 4-5$\times$ faster. The photon-memory interface, captured by the $\eta_{\mathrm{photon}}\!\cdot\!T_2$ product, is the universal bottleneck limiting both platforms.
